items.title: 14.4 Simple Harmonic Motion and Uniform Circular Motion

source_refs.note: Topic 14.4 (PDF 25-28, printed 22-25) as printed: turntable shadow, displacement, velocity and acceleration of the projection (Eqs 14.11-14.15), the Interesting Information box and Example 14.3.

blocks.text: In order to get an insight into simple S.H.M, we will co-relate it with uniform circular motion which we have already studied. The different parameters such as displacement, velocity, acceleration and time period of simple harmonic motion (S.H.M) can be understood by relating it with uniform circular motion. It has been observed that when a particle moves in a circular path, its projection on diameter of the circle executes S.H.M.
To study the simple harmonic motion, consider a turntable of radius r with a ball attached to its rim. A beam of light casts a shadow of the ball on the screen (Fig 14.4).

When the turntable rotates with constant angular speed ω, then the ball also moves along it with uniform circular motion. Its shadow on the screen oscillates executing to and fro motion across the screen in the form of simple harmonic motion, like a body attached to a spring.

blocks.alt: Light from a projector shines down on a turntable with a ball fixed to its rim; a curved arrow shows the circular motion of the ball. Below, on a screen, the ball's shadow moves to and fro, marked oscillation of ball's shadow.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.4: The oscillation of the shadow of ball on screen. The ball is attached with uniformly rotating turn table (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.4).

blocks.text: Quantitative Analysis

Consider a motion of particle P along the circumference of circle of radius x₀ with uniform angular velocity ω. Its linear velocity at point P is along the tangent (vₚ = rω). Let Q be the projection which oscillates along the diameter of circle about the mean position O. When the body is at point P its projection is at distance x from the mean position.
Instantaneous Displacement
If A is the initial position of particle P, then the angle which the radius OP sweeps out in time t is θ = ωt with OQ as shown in Fig. 14.5.

blocks.alt: A circle of radius xo with centre O and horizontal diameter ending at A. A point P on the circle moves anticlockwise with angular velocity omega; the radius OP makes the angle theta = omega t with OA. Q is the foot of the perpendicular from P on the diameter, and x = OQ is the displacement of Q from O.

Instantaneous Velocity

Considering Fig. 14.6, the line PR is the horizontal component of velocity vₚ of the particle and it is parallel to the diameter AB of the circle. Therefore, as Q vibrates horizontally, so instantaneous velocity of the point Q is horizontal component of velocity vₚ.

Its horizontal component v is drawn from P to R on the vertical diameter, parallel to BA, and an equal arrow v acts on Q along the diameter towards O. The angle between vp and the vertical is theta, and the angle between vp and PR is 90 degrees minus theta.

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: The expressions such as time period, displacement, velocity and acceleration which are true for projection of a particle are also applicable for particle moving in a circle.
Instantaneous Acceleration

Acceleration aₚ of the particle at point P is directed towards the centre of the circle as shown in Fig. 14.7. The horizontal component of aₚ is along the diameter. Thus, the acceleration of projection Q is equal to the horizontal component of aₚ.
As a = −x₀ω² (centripetal acceleration) and cos θ = x/x₀.

blocks.alt: The same circle with points A, B and C. The centripetal acceleration ap of P points along PO towards the centre. Its horizontal component a acts on Q along the diameter BA towards O. The angle theta is marked at O and at P, and x is the distance OQ.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.7: Acceleration of the point P and its horizontal component (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.7).

blocks.text: The negative sign indicates that the direction of acceleration is always directed towards the mean position.

This expression is the mathematical condition of S.H.M i.e., acceleration is directly proportional to the displacement and negative sign shows that its direction is towards mean position, therefore, it is concluded that when a particle is moving along a circumference of a circle then its projection executes S.H.M.

blocks.title: Example 14.3
blocks.problem: A 0.2 kg mass is attached to a spring with a spring constant of 10 N m⁻¹. The mass is displaced by 0.1 m from its equilibrium position and released from rest. Find: (a) acceleration at x = 0.05 m (b) velocity at x = 0.05 m
steps:
m = 0.2 kg
k = 10 N m⁻¹
x₀ = 0.1 m
Angular frequency ω = ?

(a) Acceleration at x = 0.05 m
a = −ω²x
= −(7.07 rad s⁻¹)² × 0.05 m
= −50 × 0.05
= −2.5 m s⁻²
blocks.answer: The results are: a ≈ −2.5 m s⁻², v ≈ 0.612 m s⁻¹
